speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor). The combination of a 55-year-old male with smoking history, progressive right arm weakness, sensory loss, weight loss, and diabetes is highly suggestive of an apical lung tumor compressing the brachial plexus and potentially invading the sympathetic chain (causing Horner's syndrome, though not yet mentioned). I need to confirm the extent of the mass and nerve involvement.
